meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ура, желаем вам здоровья и счастья!
examples.trans: Hurray, we wish you health and happiness!

examples.text: Желаю тебе крепкого здоровья и благополучия.
examples.trans: I wish you strong health and prosperity.

examples.text: И с днём рождения, Виктор Петрович!
examples.trans: And happy birthday, Viktor Petrovich!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'definitely'.

examples.text: Обязательно придём, Алиса уже очень готовится.
examples.trans: We will definitely come, Alisa is already getting very ready.

examples.text: И обязательно приготовьте нам большой торт.
examples.trans: And definitely prepare a big cake for us.

examples.text: Я обязательно передам его кому надо.
examples.trans: I will definitely pass it on to the right person.

приготовить.gloss: to prepare, to cook, to make

meanings.en: to prepare, to cook, to make
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (root 'готовить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to prepare', forming an aspectual pair with 'готовить'.

examples.text: Так что приготовьте обед очень быстро.
examples.trans: So prepare lunch very quickly.

examples.text: И обязательно приготовьте нам большой торт.
examples.trans: And definitely prepare a big cake for us.

examples.text: Герман Михайлович, приготовьте всё на высшем уровне!
examples.trans: German Mikhailovich, prepare everything at the highest level!

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'big', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Спасибо большое, друзья, мне очень приятно.
examples.trans: Thank you very much, friends, I am very pleased.

examples.text: Ой, спасибо большое, Герман Михайлович!
examples.trans: Oh, thank you very much, German Mikhailovich!

examples.text: И обязательно приготовьте нам большой торт.
examples.trans: And definitely prepare a big cake for us.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'cake', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: И обязательно приготовьте нам большой торт.
examples.trans: And definitely prepare a big cake for us.

examples.text: Ваш торт не такой плохой.
examples.trans: Your cake isn't so bad.

examples.text: Она испекла вкусный торт.
examples.trans: She baked a delicious cake.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to be afraid'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Боюсь, у нас не хватит столько свечей!
examples.trans: I am afraid we will not have enough candles for that!

examples.text: Нам здесь бояться некого.
examples.trans: We have nobody to fear here.

examples.text: Я не боюсь.
examples.trans: I'm not afraid.

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to be enough', forming an aspectual pair with 'хватать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Боюсь, у нас не хватит столько свечей!
examples.trans: I am afraid we will not have enough candles for that!

examples.text: Денег не хватило.
examples.trans: There wasn't enough money.

examples.text: Жвачку? Денег не хватило.
examples.trans: Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'so much'.

examples.text: Боюсь, у нас не хватит столько свечей!
examples.trans: I am afraid we will not have enough candles for that!

examples.text: Не думала, что у тебя столько друзей.
examples.trans: I did not think that you had so many friends.

examples.text: Там столько ошибок!
examples.trans: There are so many mistakes there!

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'candle', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Боюсь, у нас не хватит столько свечей!
examples.trans: I am afraid we will not have enough candles for that!

examples.text: Я приношу бутылку шампанского и свечи.
examples.trans: I'll bring a bottle of champagne and candles.

examples.text: На столе горят свечи.
examples.trans: Candles are burning on the table.
